131|def _render_items(rendered: list[str]) -> str:
132|    """One missing/unexpected list in the pin 10 feedback format."""
133|    if not rendered:
134|        return "none"
135|    text = ", ".join(rendered[:10])
136|    if len(rendered) > 10:
137|        text += f", and {len(rendered) - 10} more"
138|    return text

141|def _failed_feedback_lines(
142|    n: int, vscorecard: Any, scenarios: list[Any],
143|) -> list[str]:
144|    """Pin 10 feedback lines for a failed version, rebuilt by the test."""
145|    from fleetsre.harness.replay import T0
146|
147|    results = {r.scenario_id: r for r in vscorecard.results}
148|    visible = [s for s in scenarios if not s.holdout]
149|    passed = sum(1 for s in visible if results[s.id].passed)
150|    lines = [(
151|        f"Version {n} failed the scorecard. "
152|        f"{passed} of {len(visible)} visible scenarios passed."
153|    )]
154|    for scenario in visible:
155|        result = results[scenario.id]
156|        if result.passed:
157|            continue
158|        missing = []
159|        for kind, deployment, tripwire in result.missing:
160|            within = _within_seconds(
161|                scenario, kind, tripwire, deployment
162|            )
163|            if kind == "trip":
164|                missing.append(
165|                    f"trip {tripwire} on {deployment} "
166|                    f"within {within} s of the fault"
167|                )
168|            else:
169|                missing.append(
170|                    f"recovery {tripwire} on {deployment} "
171|                    f"within {within} s of the fault clearing"
172|                )
173|        unexpected = []
174|        for event in result.unexpected:
175|            offset = int((event.at - T0).total_seconds())
176|            unexpected.append(
177|                f"{event.kind} {event.tripwire} on {event.deployment} "
178|                f"at +{offset} s"
179|            )
180|        lines.append(
181|            f"{scenario.id}: missing {_render_items(missing)}; "
182|            f"unexpected {_render_items(unexpected)}"
183|        )
184|    return lines

187|def _user_texts(request: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
188|    """Text of the developer and user input items of a model request."""
189|    texts = []
190|    for item in request.get("input", []):
191|        if not isinstance(item, dict):
192|            continue
193|        if item.get("role") not in ("developer", "user"):
194|            continue
195|        content = item.get("content", "")
196|        if isinstance(content, str):
197|            texts.append(content)
198|        elif isinstance(content, list):
199|            texts.append(" ".join(
200|                part.get("text", "") for part in content
201|                if isinstance(part, dict)
202|            ))
203|        else:
204|            texts.append(str(content))
205|    return texts

88|
89|    The key also carries the scenario IDs: T21 renames the holdouts, and
90|    the renamed run must score fresh rather than reuse the cached result.
91|    Never a fabricated Scorecard (d6b-pins 5).
92|    """

95|    canonical = json.dumps(
96|        contract.model_dump(mode="json"),
97|        sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
98|    )
99|    key = canonical + "|" + "|".join(s.id for s in scenarios)
100|    if key not in _SCORECARD_CACHE:
101|        _SCORECARD_CACHE[key] = scorecard(contract, scenarios)

114|def _within_seconds(
115|    scenario: Any, kind: str, tripwire: str, deployment_id: str,
116|) -> int:
117|    """Deadline of a missing item, read from the scenario's expected."""
118|    env = deployment_id.split("/", 1)[1]
119|    items = (
120|        scenario.expected.trips
121|        if kind == "trip" else scenario.expected.recoveries
122|    )

132|    """One missing/unexpected list in the pin 10 feedback format."""
133|    if not rendered:
134|        return "none"

141|def _failed_feedback_lines(
142|    n: int, vscorecard: Any, scenarios: list[Any],
143|) -> list[str]:
144|    """Pin 10 feedback lines for a failed version, rebuilt by the test."""
145|    from fleetsre.harness.replay import T0
146|
147|    results = {r.scenario_id: r for r in vscorecard.results}
148|    visible = [s for s in scenarios if not s.holdout]
149|    passed = sum(1 for s in visible if results[s.id].passed)
150|    lines = [(
151|        f"Version {n} failed the scorecard. "
152|        f"{passed} of {len(visible)} visible scenarios passed."
153|    )]
154|    for scenario in visible:
155|        result = results[scenario.id]
156|        if result.passed:
157|            continue
158|        missing = []
159|        for kind, deployment, tripwire in result.missing:
160|            within = _within_seconds(
161|                scenario, kind, tripwire, deployment
162|            )
163|            if kind == "trip":
164|                missing.append(
165|                    f"trip {tripwire} on {deployment} "
166|                    f"within {within} s of the fault"
167|                )
168|            else:
169|                missing.append(
170|                    f"recovery {tripwire} on {deployment} "
171|                    f"within {within} s of the fault clearing"
172|                )
173|        unexpected = []
174|        for event in result.unexpected:
175|            offset = int((event.at - T0).total_seconds())
176|            unexpected.append(
177|                f"{event.kind} {event.tripwire} on {event.deployment} "
178|                f"at +{offset} s"
179|            )
180|        lines.append(
181|            f"{scenario.id}: missing {_render_items(missing)}; "
182|            f"unexpected {_render_items(unexpected)}"
183|        )
184|    return lines

7|  One deployment per tenant. A connector instance in the SOAR python container polls the tenant's
8|  workspace every intervalSeconds, maps each new incident to an AlertInfo and hands it to ingestion
9|  in the etl container, which writes one alert.ingested entry per alert. Tenants differ widely in

1|# Contract author
2|
3|You write the monitoring contract for one service of a multi-tenant SOAR fleet. The user message gives you:
4|- the service brief;
5|- sample log entries;
6|- the contract JSON schema;
7|- how many versions you have.
8|
9|## How you are graded
10|
11|Deterministic code grades the contract; nobody reads your reasoning. A chaos harness generates log streams for many scenarios and replays them through an evaluator running your tripwires. The scenarios include:
12|- faults on some tenants, with healthy tenants alongside;
13|- quiet tenants;
14|- transient noise;
15|- faults that clear.
16|
17|A contract passes only if, in every scenario:
18|- every expected trip and recovery happens within its deadline;
19|- nothing else trips.
20|
21|That means 100% of expected events and zero false positives. Some scenarios are held out: you never see them, and they must pass too. Write for how the service actually behaves, as the brief and samples describe it, not for the feedback alone.
22|
23|## Output
24|
25|- Reply with one JSON object: the whole contract. No prose and no code fences.
26|- Follow the schema exactly. The platform sets `service`, `version` and `provenance`.
27|- Write exactly one tripwire per check in the brief's `checks`: use its `id` and its `component`, and add no other tripwires.
28|- Use the brief's component IDs, kinds and `logs` routing, its parameter names and its event names, as given.
29|- Refer to a deployment parameter as `"${name}"`, and declare every parameter you use in `parameters`.
30|- Give every tripwire a one-sentence `description` of what it catches.
31|
32|## How the evaluator reads a contract
33|
34|A deployment is the service on one tenant. Log entries reach a component by `logs.container_name` and the `logs.match` labels, and a deployment by `logs.deploymentBy`. The evaluator ticks every 15 seconds, and each deployment is armed at the start of a scenario.
35|
36|- **cadence** (`event`, `intervalSeconds`, `maxSilentIntervals`).
37|  - It tracks the latest timestamp of the named heartbeat event.
38|  - It trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`, measured from the last heartbeat (or from arming, if none has arrived yet).
39|  - It recovers on the first heartbeat that ends the silence.
40|  - Detection takes about that window plus up to one tick.
41|- **synthetic** (`everyMinutes`, `deadlineSeconds`).
42|  - The platform plants a canary alert upstream every `everyMinutes`, starting `everyMinutes` after arming.
43|  - It trips when a canary is not seen by its deadline; a canary seen exactly at the deadline is in time.
44|  - A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next one seen in time does.
45|  - After a break, the worst-case detection is about `everyMinutes × 60 + deadlineSeconds`.
46|- **schema** (`event`, `field` as a dotted path, plus the value checks and filters the schema allows: `type`, `enum`, `required`, `where`, `consecutive`, `recoverAfter`).
47|  - Only entries whose `jsonPayload.event` equals `event`, and that match `where`, are checked. Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset anything.
48|  - It trips after `consecutive` violating entries in a row, and recovers after `recoverAfter` valid entries in a row (default `consecutive`).
49|- **errorSignature** (`minSeverity`, `windowRuns`, `threshold`).
50|  - A run is one `runId`. Its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when the run completes.
51|  - It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` completed runs are at or above `minSeverity`.
52|  - It recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
53|  - `threshold` must not exceed `windowRuns`.
54|- **changePoint** (`durationSeconds`, `overrides`).
55|  - After an approved fix, the platform applies `overrides` to the changed component's tripwires for `durationSeconds`, so a fix that did not work is caught quickly. Cadence re-arms when the window starts.
56|  - Each override key must be a tripwire ID, and each overridden field must be in that tripwire's `spec`.
57|
58|## What to get right
59|
60|- **Quiet is not broken.** Some tenants ingest only a few alerts an hour. Judge liveness from heartbeats that happen on a schedule, never from alert volume.
61|- **Noise is not failure.** Isolated warnings and errors are normal. Page on sustained failure. A threshold that is too low pages on noise; one that is too high, or a window that is too long, detects too late.
62|- **Every expected trip has a deadline**, measured from the fault, and every expected recovery has one measured from the fault clearing. Work out your worst-case detection time for each tripwire.
63|- **Allowed values must include every legitimate value.** If healthy traffic can carry a value, an enum that omits it trips on healthy traffic.
64|- **Recovery is graded too.** A tripwire that never recovers, or recovers on the wrong signal, fails scenarios where the fault clears.
65|
66|## Feedback
67|
68|After a version fails, the next message says why. It is one of:
69|- **a loader error:** fix the field it names;
70|- **a scorecard failure:** each failing visible scenario, with `missing` (expected events that did not happen in time, with their deadline) and `unexpected` (events that happened and should not have, with the time since the scenario started). A late event appears in both lists;
71|- **"a held-out scenario failed":** nothing more. Every visible scenario passed, so look for traffic your contract would mishandle that the visible scenarios did not exercise: noise, quiet tenants, recoveries, and values close to your thresholds.
72|
73|Change what the feedback points to, and keep what already passes. Reply each time with the whole revised contract.

1|# Service brief for contract authoring (D6b). Human-owned: drafted by Claude, reviewed by Rixon.
2|# Must not contain any scenario content or fault type identifier (d6b-pins 11, T12).
3|service: alert-ingestion
4|version: 1.0.0
5|summary: >-
6|  Ingests security incidents from each tenant's Microsoft Sentinel workspace into Google SecOps SOAR.
7|  One deployment per tenant. A connector instance in the SOAR python container polls the tenant's
8|  workspace every intervalSeconds, maps each new incident to an AlertInfo and hands it to ingestion
9|  in the etl container, which writes one alert.ingested entry per alert. Tenants differ widely in
10|  volume: some ingest over a hundred alerts an hour, others only a few. The connector's API status
11|  stays LIVE while the instance is enabled, whether or not it is working.
12|components:
13|  - id: connector
14|    kind: connectorInstance
15|    description: The tenant's Sentinel connector instance, running in the python container.
16|    logs:
17|      container_name: python
18|      match: [connector_name, connector_instance]
19|      deploymentBy: labels.connector_instance
20|  - id: ingestion
21|    kind: etlFlow
22|    description: Ingestion of the connector's alerts, in the etl container. One entry per alert.
23|    logs:
24|      container_name: etl
25|      match: [correlation_id]
26|      deploymentBy: jsonPayload.environment
27|parameters:
28|  expectedAlertsPerHour:
29|    type: number
30|    description: The tenant's typical alert volume. Supplied per deployment.
31|  intervalSeconds:
32|    type: integer
33|    description: The connector's polling interval in seconds. Supplied per deployment.
34|events:
35|  - event: connector.run.started
36|    container: python
37|    description: A connector run began.
38|  - event: connector.run.completed
39|    container: python
40|    description: >-
41|      A connector run ended. Every run ends with this entry, including a run that failed, so it is
42|      the connector's heartbeat. jsonPayload.alertsFetched is the number of alerts fetched.
43|  - event: connector.run.warning
44|    container: python
45|    description: The run hit a problem it worked around (severity WARNING). Written before connector.run.completed.
46|  - event: connector.run.error
47|    container: python
48|    description: The run failed (severity ERROR). Written before connector.run.completed.
49|  - event: alert.ingested
50|    container: etl
51|    description: >-
52|      One alert reached SOAR. jsonPayload.alert holds name, ticket_id, rule_generator, priority,
53|      device_vendor, device_product, environment, start_time, end_time and canary.
54|checks:
55|  - id: dead-connector
56|    component: connector
57|    detects: >-
58|      The connector stops running. The API keeps reporting LIVE; only the missing runs show it.
59|  - id: canary
60|    component: ingestion
61|    detects: >-
62|      Alerts stop reaching SOAR end to end while every connector run looks normal. The platform can
63|      plant a canary incident upstream on a schedule; it is seen when an alert.ingested entry has
64|      alert.canary true and alert.ticket_id equal to the planted incident's ID.
65|  - id: priority-shape
66|    component: ingestion
67|    detects: >-
68|      Ingested alerts whose priority is not on Google's scale: a string, a missing value or an
69|      unlisted number. Healthy priorities are the integers -1 (Informational), 40 (Low), 60 (Medium),
70|      80 (High) and 100 (Critical). One malformed alert matters.
71|  - id: connector-errors
72|    component: connector
73|    detects: >-
74|      The connector keeps running on schedule but most of its runs fail, for example because the
75|      upstream rejects its credential; it then fetches nothing while still reporting LIVE. Occasional
76|      failed runs are normal on a healthy connector and must not page.
77|notes:
78|  - Connector runs happen every intervalSeconds regardless of alert volume. A quiet tenant can go an hour or more without ingesting an alert.
79|  - A failed connector run writes connector.run.warning or connector.run.error first and still ends with connector.run.completed.
80|  - After an approved fix to a component, the platform applies the contract's changePoint overrides to that component's tripwires for changePoint.durationSeconds.

1|# Contract author
2|
3|You write the monitoring contract for one service of a multi-tenant SOAR fleet. The user message gives you:
4|- the service brief;
5|- sample log entries;
6|- the contract JSON schema;
7|- how many versions you have.
8|
9|## How you are graded
10|
11|Deterministic code grades the contract; nobody reads your reasoning. A chaos harness generates log streams for many scenarios and replays them through an evaluator running your tripwires. The scenarios include:
12|- faults on some tenants, with healthy tenants alongside;
13|- quiet tenants;
14|- transient noise;
15|- faults that clear.
16|
17|A contract passes only if, in every scenario:
18|- every expected trip and recovery happens within its deadline;
19|- nothing else trips.
20|
21|That means 100% of expected events and zero false positives. Some scenarios are held out: you never see them, and they must pass too. Write for how the service actually behaves, as the brief and samples describe it, not for the feedback alone.
22|
23|## Output
24|
25|- Reply with one JSON object: the whole contract. No prose and no code fences.
26|- Follow the schema exactly. The platform sets `service`, `version` and `provenance`.
27|- Write exactly one tripwire per check in the brief's `checks`: use its `id` and its `component`, and add no other tripwires.
28|- Use the brief's component IDs, kinds and `logs` routing, its parameter names and its event names, as given.
29|- Refer to a deployment parameter as `"${name}"`, and declare every parameter you use in `parameters`.
30|- Give every tripwire a one-sentence `description` of what it catches.
31|
32|## How the evaluator reads a contract
33|
34|A deployment is the service on one tenant. Log entries reach a component by `logs.container_name` and the `logs.match` labels, and a deployment by `logs.deploymentBy`. The evaluator ticks every 15 seconds, and each deployment is armed at the start of a scenario.
35|
36|- **cadence** (`event`, `intervalSeconds`, `maxSilentIntervals`).
37|  - It tracks the latest timestamp of the named heartbeat event.
38|  - It trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`, measured from the last heartbeat (or from arming, if none has arrived yet).
39|  - It recovers on the first heartbeat that ends the silence.
40|  - Detection takes about that window plus up to one tick.
41|- **synthetic** (`everyMinutes`, `deadlineSeconds`).
42|  - The platform plants a canary alert upstream every `everyMinutes`, starting `everyMinutes` after arming.
43|  - It trips when a canary is not seen by its deadline; a canary seen exactly at the deadline is in time.
44|  - A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next one seen in time does.
45|  - After a break, the worst-case detection is about `everyMinutes × 60 + deadlineSeconds`.
46|- **schema** (`event`, `field` as a dotted path, plus the value checks and filters the schema allows: `type`, `enum`, `required`, `where`, `consecutive`, `recoverAfter`).
47|  - Only entries whose `jsonPayload.event` equals `event`, and that match `where`, are checked. Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset anything.
48|  - It trips after `consecutive` violating entries in a row, and recovers after `recoverAfter` valid entries in a row (default `consecutive`).
49|- **errorSignature** (`minSeverity`, `windowRuns`, `threshold`).
50|  - A run is one `runId`. Its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when the run completes.
51|  - It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` completed runs are at or above `minSeverity`.
52|  - It recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
53|  - `threshold` must not exceed `windowRuns`.
54|- **changePoint** (`durationSeconds`, `overrides`).
55|  - After an approved fix, the platform applies `overrides` to the changed component's tripwires for `durationSeconds`, so a fix that did not work is caught quickly. Cadence re-arms when the window starts.
56|  - Each override key must be a tripwire ID, and each overridden field must be in that tripwire's `spec`.
57|
58|## What to get right
59|
60|- **Quiet is not broken.** Some tenants ingest only a few alerts an hour. Judge liveness from heartbeats that happen on a schedule, never from alert volume.
61|- **Noise is not failure.** Isolated warnings and errors are normal. Page on sustained failure. A threshold that is too low pages on noise; one that is too high, or a window that is too long, detects too late.
62|- **Every expected trip has a deadline**, measured from the fault, and every expected recovery has one measured from the fault clearing. Work out your worst-case detection time for each tripwire.
63|- **Allowed values must include every legitimate value.** If healthy traffic can carry a value, an enum that omits it trips on healthy traffic.
64|- **Recovery is graded too.** A tripwire that never recovers, or recovers on the wrong signal, fails scenarios where the fault clears.
65|
66|## Feedback
67|
68|After a version fails, the next message says why. It is one of:
69|- **a loader error:** fix the field it names;
70|- **a scorecard failure:** each failing visible scenario, with `missing` (expected events that did not happen in time, with their deadline) and `unexpected` (events that happened and should not have, with the time since the scenario started). A late event appears in both lists;
71|- **"a held-out scenario failed":** nothing more. Every visible scenario passed, so look for traffic your contract would mishandle that the visible scenarios did not exercise: noise, quiet tenants, recoveries, and values close to your thresholds.
72|
73|Change what the feedback points to, and keep what already passes. Reply each time with the whole revised contract.

1|"""D4 replay harness: run one chaos scenario against a contract."""
2|
3|from dataclasses import dataclass, field
4|from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
5|from pathlib import Path
6|
7|from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
8|from fleetsre.contracts import Contract
9|from fleetsre.evaluator.canary import CanaryScheduler
10|from fleetsre.evaluator.engine import Evaluator, TripEvent
11|from fleetsre.harness.scenario import Expected, Scenario
12|from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
13|from fleetsre.mock.world import World
14|from fleetsre.ports import MemorySink
15|from fleetsre.registry import deployments_from_fleet
16|
17|T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
18|
19|
20|@dataclass
21|class ScenarioResult:
22|    """Result of replaying one scenario.
23|
24|    latencies maps (kind, deployment_id, tripwire) to seconds, where kind is
25|    "trip" or "recovery" and deployment_id is "<service>/<environment>".
26|    missing holds (kind, deployment_id, tripwire) for expected items with no
27|    actual match within withinSeconds. unexpected holds actual events matched
28|    by no expected item (mustNotTrip violations included).
29|    """
30|
31|    scenario_id: str
32|    expected: Expected
33|    actual: list[TripEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
34|    latencies: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = field(default_factory=dict)
35|    missing: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = field(default_factory=list)
36|    unexpected: list[TripEvent] = field(default_factory=list)
37|    passed: bool = False
38|
39|
40|def _fleet_path() -> Path:
41|    return (
42|        Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
43|        / "fixtures"
44|        / "fleet.yaml"
45|    )
46|
47|
48|def _latest_fault_at(
49|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
50|) -> datetime | None:
51|    best: datetime | None = None
52|    for fault in scenario.faults:
53|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.at)
54|        if fault.environment == environment and ref <= at:
55|            if best is None or ref > best:
56|                best = ref
57|    return best
58|
59|
60|def _latest_clear_at(
61|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
62|) -> datetime | None:
63|    best: datetime | None = None
64|    for fault in scenario.faults:
65|        if fault.environment != environment or fault.clearAt is None:
66|            continue
67|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.clearAt)
68|        if ref <= at and (best is None or ref > best):
69|            best = ref
70|    if best is not None:
71|        return best
72|    return _latest_fault_at(scenario, environment, at)
73|
74|
75|def replay_tick(
76|    clock: SimClock,
77|    scheduler: CanaryScheduler,
78|    world: World,
79|    sink: MemorySink,
80|    evaluator: Evaluator,
81|    consumed: int,
82|    tick_at: datetime,
83|) -> tuple[list[TripEvent], int]:
84|    """Run one replay tick at `tick_at` (D4 semantics 1).
85|
86|    Shared by run_scenario and the D6a control loop (d6a-pins 9):
87|    scheduler, world, ingest new sink entries in write order, then the
88|    evaluator tick. Returns the tick's events and the new consume count.
89|    """
90|    clock.set(tick_at)
91|    scheduler.tick()
92|    world.step_until(tick_at)
93|    events: list[TripEvent] = []
94|    entries = sink.entries
95|    while consumed < len(entries):
96|        events.extend(evaluator.ingest(entries[consumed]))
97|        consumed += 1
98|    events.extend(evaluator.tick())
99|    return events, consumed
100|
101|
102|def run_scenario(
103|    contract: Contract, scenario: Scenario, *, tick_seconds: int = 15
104|) -> ScenarioResult:
105|    """Replay one scenario against its contract on a SimClock."""
106|    fleet = load_fleet(_fleet_path())
107|    clock = SimClock(T0)
108|    sink = MemorySink()
109|    world = World(fleet, scenario.seed, clock, sink)
110|    items: list[dict[str, object]] = []
111|    for fault in scenario.faults:
112|        item: dict[str, object] = {
113|            "at": fault.at,
114|            "type": fault.type,
115|            "environment": fault.environment,
116|            "params": dict(fault.params),
117|        }
118|        target = getattr(fault, "target", None)
119|        if target is not None:
120|            item["target"] = target
121|        if fault.clearAt is not None:
122|            item["clearAt"] = fault.clearAt
123|        items.append(item)
124|    world.schedule(items)
125|    deployments = deployments_from_fleet(fleet, contract, scenario.deployments)
126|    evaluator = Evaluator([contract], deployments, clock)
127|    scheduler = CanaryScheduler(world, evaluator, [contract], clock)
128|    actual: list[TripEvent] = []
129|    consumed = 0
130|    steps = scenario.durationSeconds // tick_seconds
131|    for step in range(steps + 1):
132|        tick_at = T0 + timedelta(seconds=step * tick_seconds)
133|        events, consumed = replay_tick(
134|            clock, scheduler, world, sink, evaluator, consumed, tick_at
135|        )
136|        actual.extend(events)
137|
138|    latencies: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = {}
139|    missing: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
140|    unexpected: list[TripEvent] = []
141|    matched = [False] * len(actual)
142|    by_key: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[int]] = {}
143|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
144|        by_key.setdefault(
145|            (event.kind, event.deployment, event.tripwire), []
146|        ).append(index)
147|    for trip in scenario.expected.trips:
148|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{trip.deployment}"
149|        key = ("trip", dep_id, trip.tripwire)
150|        hit = False
151|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
152|            if matched[index]:
153|                continue
154|            ref = _latest_fault_at(
155|                scenario, trip.deployment, actual[index].at
156|            )
157|            if ref is None:
158|                continue
159|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
160|            if 0 <= latency <= trip.withinSeconds:
161|                matched[index] = True
162|                latencies[key] = latency
163|                hit = True
164|                break
165|        if not hit:
166|            missing.append(key)
167|    for recovery in scenario.expected.recoveries:
168|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{recovery.deployment}"
169|        key = ("recovery", dep_id, recovery.tripwire)
170|        hit = False
171|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
172|            if matched[index]:
173|                continue
174|            ref = _latest_clear_at(
175|                scenario, recovery.deployment, actual[index].at
176|            )
177|            if ref is None:
178|                continue
179|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
180|            if 0 <= latency <= recovery.withinSeconds:
181|                matched[index] = True
182|                latencies[key] = latency
183|                hit = True
184|                break
185|        if not hit:
186|            missing.append(key)
187|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
188|        if not matched[index]:
189|            unexpected.append(event)
190|    return ScenarioResult(
191|        scenario_id=scenario.id,
192|        expected=scenario.expected,
193|        actual=actual,
194|        latencies=latencies,
195|        missing=missing,
196|        unexpected=unexpected,
197|        passed=(not missing and not unexpected),
198|    )

48|def _latest_fault_at(
49|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
50|) -> datetime | None:
51|    best: datetime | None = None
52|    for fault in scenario.faults:
53|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.at)
54|        if fault.environment == environment and ref <= at:
55|            if best is None or ref > best:
56|                best = ref
57|    return best

60|def _latest_clear_at(
61|    scenario: Scenario, environment: str, at: datetime
62|) -> datetime | None:
63|    best: datetime | None = None
64|    for fault in scenario.faults:
65|        if fault.environment != environment or fault.clearAt is None:
66|            continue
67|        ref = T0 + timedelta(seconds=fault.clearAt)
68|        if ref <= at and (best is None or ref > best):
69|            best = ref
70|    if best is not None:
71|        return best
72|    return _latest_fault_at(scenario, environment, at)

75|def replay_tick(
76|    clock: SimClock,
77|    scheduler: CanaryScheduler,
78|    world: World,
79|    sink: MemorySink,
80|    evaluator: Evaluator,
81|    consumed: int,
82|    tick_at: datetime,
83|) -> tuple[list[TripEvent], int]:
84|    """Run one replay tick at `tick_at` (D4 semantics 1).
85|
86|    Shared by run_scenario and the D6a control loop (d6a-pins 9):
87|    scheduler, world, ingest new sink entries in write order, then the
88|    evaluator tick. Returns the tick's events and the new consume count.
89|    """
90|    clock.set(tick_at)
91|    scheduler.tick()
92|    world.step_until(tick_at)
93|    events: list[TripEvent] = []
94|    entries = sink.entries
95|    while consumed < len(entries):
96|        events.extend(evaluator.ingest(entries[consumed]))
97|        consumed += 1
98|    events.extend(evaluator.tick())
99|    return events, consumed
100|
101|
102|def run_scenario(
103|    contract: Contract, scenario: Scenario, *, tick_seconds: int = 15
104|) -> ScenarioResult:
105|    """Replay one scenario against its contract on a SimClock."""
106|    fleet = load_fleet(_fleet_path())
107|    clock = SimClock(T0)
108|    sink = MemorySink()
109|    world = World(fleet, scenario.seed, clock, sink)
110|    items: list[dict[str, object]] = []
111|    for fault in scenario.faults:
112|        item: dict[str, object] = {
113|            "at": fault.at,
114|            "type": fault.type,
115|            "environment": fault.environment,
116|            "params": dict(fault.params),
117|        }
118|        target = getattr(fault, "target", None)
119|        if target is not None:
120|            item["target"] = target
121|        if fault.clearAt is not None:
122|            item["clearAt"] = fault.clearAt
123|        items.append(item)
124|    world.schedule(items)
125|    deployments = deployments_from_fleet(fleet, contract, scenario.deployments)
126|    evaluator = Evaluator([contract], deployments, clock)
127|    scheduler = CanaryScheduler(world, evaluator, [contract], clock)
128|    actual: list[TripEvent] = []
129|    consumed = 0
130|    steps = scenario.durationSeconds // tick_seconds
131|    for step in range(steps + 1):
132|        tick_at = T0 + timedelta(seconds=step * tick_seconds)
133|        events, consumed = replay_tick(
134|            clock, scheduler, world, sink, evaluator, consumed, tick_at
135|        )
136|        actual.extend(events)
137|
138|    latencies: dict[tuple[str, str, str], float] = {}
139|    missing: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []
140|    unexpected: list[TripEvent] = []
141|    matched = [False] * len(actual)
142|    by_key: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[int]] = {}
143|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
144|        by_key.setdefault(
145|            (event.kind, event.deployment, event.tripwire), []
146|        ).append(index)
147|    for trip in scenario.expected.trips:
148|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{trip.deployment}"
149|        key = ("trip", dep_id, trip.tripwire)
150|        hit = False
151|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
152|            if matched[index]:
153|                continue
154|            ref = _latest_fault_at(
155|                scenario, trip.deployment, actual[index].at
156|            )
157|            if ref is None:
158|                continue
159|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
160|            if 0 <= latency <= trip.withinSeconds:
161|                matched[index] = True
162|                latencies[key] = latency
163|                hit = True
164|                break
165|        if not hit:
166|            missing.append(key)
167|    for recovery in scenario.expected.recoveries:
168|        dep_id = f"{scenario.service}/{recovery.deployment}"
169|        key = ("recovery", dep_id, recovery.tripwire)
170|        hit = False
171|        for index in by_key.get(key, []):
172|            if matched[index]:
173|                continue
174|            ref = _latest_clear_at(
175|                scenario, recovery.deployment, actual[index].at
176|            )
177|            if ref is None:
178|                continue
179|            latency = (actual[index].at - ref).total_seconds()
180|            if 0 <= latency <= recovery.withinSeconds:
181|                matched[index] = True
182|                latencies[key] = latency
183|                hit = True
184|                break
185|        if not hit:
186|            missing.append(key)
187|    for index, event in enumerate(actual):
188|        if not matched[index]:
189|            unexpected.append(event)
190|    return ScenarioResult(
191|        scenario_id=scenario.id,
192|        expected=scenario.expected,
193|        actual=actual,
194|        latencies=latencies,
195|        missing=missing,
196|        unexpected=unexpected,
197|        passed=(not missing and not unexpected),
198|    )

1|# D5 pins
2|
3|Interfaces and semantics of the D5 investigator as built (PRs #22–#27). `deliverables.md` §D5 and `spec.md` §6 summarise them; this file has the detail and wins where they differ. `tests/acceptance/d5/` encodes the testable rules; `tests/unit/` covers the rest.
4|
5|## Interfaces
6|
7|1. **`fleetsre/ports.py`.**
8|   - `LogQuery` protocol: `entries(start, end) -> list[LogEntry]`, `get(insert_id) -> LogEntry | None`; `MemoryLogQuery(sink)`.
9|   - `ChronicleClient` protocol: `get(name)`, `list_connector_logs(name, page_size)`, `list_job_logs(name, page_size)`, `execute_test(name)`, `patch(name, body, update_mask)`, `run_on_demand(name, body)`, `set_logs_collection(name, enabled)`, and an `identity` attribute. Returns parsed JSON or raises `ChronicleError(status, body)` carrying the Google error body.
10|   - `StateStore` protocol: `record_trip(event)`, `record_change(deployment, record)`, `trip_history(deployment) -> list[dict]`; `MemoryStateStore`.
11|2. **`fleetsre/adapters/chronicle_http.py`.** `ChronicleHttpClient(http: httpx.Client, identity: str)` sends `X-Fleetsre-Identity` (dev auth; ID tokens come in D7).
12|3. **`fleetsre/registry.py`.**
13|   - `Registry(contracts, deployments, scorecards=None)` with `contract(service)`, `deployments(service)`, `deployment(id)`, `scorecard(service)` and `route(entry) -> list[(deployment ID, component ID)]`, using the evaluator's routing (D4 semantics item 5). D6 adds `apply_contract`.
14|   - `Deployment.resource_names` maps component ID → full Chronicle resource name, plus `"integrationInstance"`. `deployments_from_fleet` computes it from the fleet; `Deployment.resources` keeps its D4 meaning (routing).
15|4. **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may import `fleetsre.registry`, `contracts`, `logmodel`, `ports`, `clock` and `evaluator.tripwires`. It must not reach `google`, `fleetsre.adapters` or `fleetsre.mock`, transitively included. `.importlinter` sets `exclude_type_checking_imports = True`.
16|5. **`ToolSet(log_query, chronicle, state, registry, *, clock, verification=True)`.**
17|   - `call(name, args, session, *, call_id=None)` always returns `{"callId": <id>, "result": <dict>}`: exactly what reaches the model.
18|   - A refusal's result is `{"error": str, "problems": [str]}`. `call` never raises; an internal error is a refusal with rule `tool.error`.
19|   - With `call_id=None` the ToolSet assigns `local-<n>`.
20|   - Every call is stored in `session.calls[call_id]` as a `CallRecord(tool, args, result, verdict, problems, turn)`.
21|   - The gates get the incident through `Incident.reconstruct(session.incident_id, registry, now)`, which parses the ID against the registry's services, environments and tripwire IDs (never by splitting on `-`).
22|   - Read-tool output schemas live in `fleetsre/sre/schemas.py` as `READ_TOOL_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`.
23|6. **`Incident`** has `id`, `deployment`, `tripwire`, `opened_at`, `trip_event`, `service`, `component`, `resources` and `siblings`.
24|   - `resources` comes from `Deployment.resource_names`; `siblings` holds deployment IDs.
25|   - `Incident.from_trip(event, registry, now)` sets `id = f"inc-{service}-{environment}-{tripwire}-{at:%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"`.
26|   - `render_incident(incident, registry) -> str` builds the first user message: incident ID, deployment, `Component: <ID> (the tripped tripwire's component)`, every component of the service with its kind and full resource name, every tripwire with its component, the tripped tripwire's type and spec with `${param}` resolved (never the description text), trip reason, trip evidence insertIds, trippedAt, now, sibling IDs and budgets.
27|7. **`Evidence`** gains `deployment: str | None`. For a log source, `value` is `entry.model_dump(mode="json")`.
28|8. **`Session`** is JSON round-trippable.
29|   - Typed fields: `hypotheses: dict[str, Hypothesis]`, `evidence: dict[str, Evidence]`, `calls: dict[str, CallRecord]`.
30|   - Also: `turn`, `history` (input items), `segment_start_turn`, `turn_limit`, `read_limit`, `token_limit`, `segment_reads`, `segment_tokens`, `refused_submissions`, `resumed_at_turns`, `transcript_id` and `plan`.
31|   - `status` is `running | submitted | needs_input`.
32|   - `SessionStore`: `save`, `load`, `append_transcript(transcript_id, record)`, `transcript(transcript_id)`. Implementations: `MemorySessionStore()` (`fleetsre/sre/session.py`) and `SqliteSessionStore(path)` (`fleetsre/adapters/sqlite_state.py`).
33|9. **`investigate(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, max_turns=24, max_read_calls=12, max_tokens=400_000)`.**
34|   - With no saved session it starts one. With a saved `running` session it continues it with the budgets passed. With a saved `submitted` or `needs_input` session it raises `ValueError`.
35|   - `resume(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, message, extra_turns=8, extra_reads=4)` raises `ValueError` unless the saved session is `needs_input`.
36|   - Both return `InvestigationResult(diagnosis, status, reason, transcript_id, turns, read_calls, tokens, refusals)`. `status` is `submitted`, with `reason` the submitted action type (`propose` or `none`), or `needs_input` with a reason from pin 15. For `escalated`, `diagnosis` is set.
37|10. **`ModelGateway(config, transport, *, sleep=time.sleep)`.**
38|    - `ModelGateway.respond(role, input_items, tools)` returns `ModelResponse(output, usage)`; `tools` may be `None`.
39|    - `Transport.create(request: dict) -> dict` raises `TransportError(status)`.
40|    - `ScriptedTransport(responses)` records `.requests`; an item `{"_error": <status>}` raises `TransportError`.
41|    - `GatewayConfig.prices`: per model, USD per 1M tokens (`input`, `cached_input`, `output`).
42|    - `OpenAITransport(*, api_key, base_url)` calls the OpenAI SDK's `responses.create` with SDK `max_retries=0` and `timeout=120`. A timeout surfaces as `TransportError(504)`. The key is passed explicitly from `MODEL_API_KEY`.
43|    - The live role comes from `FLEETSRE_INVESTIGATE_MODEL` (default `muse-spark-1.3`), effort `medium`, prices from `FLEETSRE_PRICES_JSON`.
44|11. **Gate signatures.** `check_hypotheses(items)`; `check_evidence(args, session, log_query, incident, registry)`; `check_diagnosis(d, session, incident, contract, log_query, registry)`.
45|
46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.
64|
65|## Tools
66|
67|19. **`query_logs(deployment, window, filter, rationale)`.**
68|    - `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}`, relative to `clock.now()`.
69|    - `filter` is `{component?, event?, minSeverity?, runId?}`, `additionalProperties: false`. A `component` that is not a component ID of the deployment's contract is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
70|    - Returns `{"entries", "total", "truncated"}`: newest first by timestamp, at most 50. Each entry is compact: `insertId`, `timestamp`, `severity`, `labels`, `jsonPayload`, `container`.
71|    - Querying a sibling deployment marks it queried.
72|20. **`get_resource(name)`** is GET only. `name` must match an `environments`, `integrationInstances`, `connectorInstances` or `jobInstances` pattern under the fixed prefix (mocks §4.1). Anything else, including `:` custom methods and `/logs/` paths, is refused (`tool.name`) with no HTTP call. Mock errors pass through as an accepted `{"error": <Google error body>}`.
73|21. **Log and test tools.** `list_connector_logs(name)` and `list_job_logs(name)` take full resource names and return one page of 50, newest first: `{"logs", "truncated"}`. `test_integration_instance(name)` takes integration instance names only and returns the `executeTest` body.
74|22. **`compare_siblings(service, component, window)`**, where `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}` as in pin 19. For each deployment of the service it returns: runs, runs at or above WARNING, ERROR runs, the last heartbeat's timestamp and insertId, alerts ingested, and the insertId of the worst recent entry. It marks every sibling queried. An unknown component is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
75|23. **`tripwire_history(deployment)`** reads the `StateStore`. **`get_contract(service)`** returns the contract JSON with every tripwire `description` removed, plus a scorecard summary only (`passed`, `expected_hit_rate`, `false_positives`, `scenarios: <count>`), with no scenario IDs.
76|24. **Specs.** `submit_diagnosis` carries the full §6.5 schema with its `required` lists (diagnosis, action, `expectedVerification`, `openQuestions` items) and `condition` enum `["recovers_within"]`. `record_evidence`'s `source` is `{insertId}` or `{callId, field, value}`. Every schema has `additionalProperties: false` and a required `rationale` (`maxLength` 200). `update_plan(plan, rationale)` records the plan and has no gate.
77|
78|## Gates
79|
80|25. **Problem strings** take the form `<rule>: <text>`. Rules:
81|    - Order and hypotheses: `order`, `hypotheses.count`, `hypotheses.alternative`, `hypotheses.id`.
82|    - Evidence: `evidence.insert_id`, `evidence.deployment`, `evidence.future`, `evidence.call_id`, `evidence.field`, `evidence.value`, `evidence.hypothesis`, `evidence.limit`.
83|    - Diagnosis:
84|      - `diagnosis.schema`, with the JSON path of the problem (`diagnosis.schema: action: 'type' is a required property`). Argument-validation errors inside `diagnosis` use this rule, not `args.schema`.
85|      - `diagnosis.evidence`
86|      - `diagnosis.coverage`
87|      - `diagnosis.category` (includes `unknown` without `escalate`)
88|      - `diagnosis.action` (method outside the allowlist; empty `escalationSummary`)
89|      - `diagnosis.update_mask` (mask outside the method's fields, or patch keys outside the mask)
90|      - `diagnosis.resource`
91|      - `diagnosis.incident` (`incidentId` or `deployment`)
92|      - `diagnosis.component`, listing the contract's component IDs
93|      - `diagnosis.hypothesis`
94|      - `diagnosis.verification` (missing, or a tripwire not of this deployment)
95|      - `diagnosis.none_after_resume`
96|    - Other: `reads.cap`, `tool.unknown`, `tool.name`, `tool.error`, `args.schema` (with the JSON path).
97|26. **`set_hypotheses`.** Items are `{id, statement, wouldConfirm, alternative}`, all four required. IDs match `^H[1-9][0-9]*$` and are unique. 2–4 items, at least one alternative. Replacing the set keeps evidence whose hypothesis ID remains.
98|27. **`record_evidence`.**
99|    - **Log source:** the insertId exists, its timestamp is ≤ now, and it routes (via `Registry.route`) to the incident's deployment or to a sibling queried in this session (via `query_logs` on it, or `compare_siblings`). There is no other fallback.
100|    - **Tool source:** `callId` is an accepted read-tool call of this session. `field` is a dotted path into the result, where numeric segments index lists and a leading `result.` is stripped. `value` must match by JSON equality, with no coercion.
101|    - At most 3 items per hypothesis. IDs are `E<n>`, and `recordedAtTurn` is the session turn.
102|28. **`submit_diagnosis`** checks, in addition to spec §6.5:
103|    - The schema first. A schema problem always refuses, gates on or off. With gates on and no hypotheses yet, the order problem is reported first.
104|    - `incidentId` and `deployment` equal the incident's.
105|    - `component` is a component ID of the deployment's contract.
106|    - `hypothesis` is a current hypothesis.
107|    - For `propose`: a `connectorInstances.*` method needs the deployment's connector instance name, and a `jobInstances.*` method its job instance name, by exact match. The integration instance is never a valid resource. The patch keys are within `updateMask`.
108|    - `expectedVerification` is required for `propose` and `none`, and optional for `escalate`.
109|    - For `none`: an item counts as recorded after the last resume iff `recordedAtTurn > max(resumed_at_turns)`. With no resume, every item counts.
110|    - Repeated submissions to the ToolSet are allowed; the loop ends at the first accepted one.
111|29. **Category rules** (the spec §6.5 table, tightened):
112|    - `connector_stalled` / `job_stalled`: the cited log evidence includes, by insertId, the deployment's latest heartbeat at or before `trip_event.at`. The heartbeat is the event of the cadence tripwire on the contract's `connectorInstance` (`jobInstance`) component, whatever the incident's component, so a canary incident can be diagnosed `connector_stalled`.
113|    - `credential_failure`: an entry from the deployment's connector at or above WARNING, plus a `test_integration_instance` call on the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false`.
114|    - `schema_drift`: an entry that routes to the incident's deployment and for which `evaluator.tripwires.schema_violation` returns a reason. `schema_violation` applies the tripwire's `event`/`where` filters itself; `${param}` is resolved.
115|    - `job_hollow_success`: a `job.run.completed` of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0`.
116|    - `job_failing`: a `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` with `status: ERROR`, of the deployment.
117|30. **`verification=False`.** The order, hypotheses, evidence and diagnosis rules 2–5 record `wouldRefuse`, with their problems, instead of refusing. Schema problems (`args.schema`, `diagnosis.schema`) still refuse. Budgets, the read cap and stuck still apply.
118|31. **The right component** for evaluation is the tripped tripwire's component.
119|
120|## Recording and evaluation
121|
122|32. **`make record FAULT=<F>`** runs one live investigation on the scripted fixture's world and writes `fixtures/recorded/<F>.json`, containing `{fault, seed, t0, faults, incident, responses, transcript, diagnosis}`. Every `encrypted_content` value is replaced with `"<stripped>"` at record time. Committed recordings: F1, F2, F3 (#26).
123|33. **Live eval (T19/T20)** writes `evals/d5-<UTC date>.json`: per run the status, reason, turns, reads, tokens, cost, refusals by rule, tools called and diagnosis; plus the F2 probe share and, per fault, one gates-off run's outcome with its would-refuse and refused counts by rule.
124|
125|## Results (muse-spark-1.3, effort medium)
126|
127|| Run | Prompt | Correct | Notes |

1|# D5 pins
2|
3|Interfaces and semantics of the D5 investigator as built (PRs #22–#27). `deliverables.md` §D5 and `spec.md` §6 summarise them; this file has the detail and wins where they differ. `tests/acceptance/d5/` encodes the testable rules; `tests/unit/` covers the rest.
4|
5|## Interfaces
6|
7|1. **`fleetsre/ports.py`.**
8|   - `LogQuery` protocol: `entries(start, end) -> list[LogEntry]`, `get(insert_id) -> LogEntry | None`; `MemoryLogQuery(sink)`.
9|   - `ChronicleClient` protocol: `get(name)`, `list_connector_logs(name, page_size)`, `list_job_logs(name, page_size)`, `execute_test(name)`, `patch(name, body, update_mask)`, `run_on_demand(name, body)`, `set_logs_collection(name, enabled)`, and an `identity` attribute. Returns parsed JSON or raises `ChronicleError(status, body)` carrying the Google error body.
10|   - `StateStore` protocol: `record_trip(event)`, `record_change(deployment, record)`, `trip_history(deployment) -> list[dict]`; `MemoryStateStore`.
11|2. **`fleetsre/adapters/chronicle_http.py`.** `ChronicleHttpClient(http: httpx.Client, identity: str)` sends `X-Fleetsre-Identity` (dev auth; ID tokens come in D7).
12|3. **`fleetsre/registry.py`.**
13|   - `Registry(contracts, deployments, scorecards=None)` with `contract(service)`, `deployments(service)`, `deployment(id)`, `scorecard(service)` and `route(entry) -> list[(deployment ID, component ID)]`, using the evaluator's routing (D4 semantics item 5). D6 adds `apply_contract`.
14|   - `Deployment.resource_names` maps component ID → full Chronicle resource name, plus `"integrationInstance"`. `deployments_from_fleet` computes it from the fleet; `Deployment.resources` keeps its D4 meaning (routing).
15|4. **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may import `fleetsre.registry`, `contracts`, `logmodel`, `ports`, `clock` and `evaluator.tripwires`. It must not reach `google`, `fleetsre.adapters` or `fleetsre.mock`, transitively included. `.importlinter` sets `exclude_type_checking_imports = True`.
16|5. **`ToolSet(log_query, chronicle, state, registry, *, clock, verification=True)`.**
17|   - `call(name, args, session, *, call_id=None)` always returns `{"callId": <id>, "result": <dict>}`: exactly what reaches the model.
18|   - A refusal's result is `{"error": str, "problems": [str]}`. `call` never raises; an internal error is a refusal with rule `tool.error`.
19|   - With `call_id=None` the ToolSet assigns `local-<n>`.
20|   - Every call is stored in `session.calls[call_id]` as a `CallRecord(tool, args, result, verdict, problems, turn)`.
21|   - The gates get the incident through `Incident.reconstruct(session.incident_id, registry, now)`, which parses the ID against the registry's services, environments and tripwire IDs (never by splitting on `-`).
22|   - Read-tool output schemas live in `fleetsre/sre/schemas.py` as `READ_TOOL_OUTPUT_SCHEMAS`.
23|6. **`Incident`** has `id`, `deployment`, `tripwire`, `opened_at`, `trip_event`, `service`, `component`, `resources` and `siblings`.
24|   - `resources` comes from `Deployment.resource_names`; `siblings` holds deployment IDs.
25|   - `Incident.from_trip(event, registry, now)` sets `id = f"inc-{service}-{environment}-{tripwire}-{at:%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}"`.
26|   - `render_incident(incident, registry) -> str` builds the first user message: incident ID, deployment, `Component: <ID> (the tripped tripwire's component)`, every component of the service with its kind and full resource name, every tripwire with its component, the tripped tripwire's type and spec with `${param}` resolved (never the description text), trip reason, trip evidence insertIds, trippedAt, now, sibling IDs and budgets.
27|7. **`Evidence`** gains `deployment: str | None`. For a log source, `value` is `entry.model_dump(mode="json")`.
28|8. **`Session`** is JSON round-trippable.
29|   - Typed fields: `hypotheses: dict[str, Hypothesis]`, `evidence: dict[str, Evidence]`, `calls: dict[str, CallRecord]`.
30|   - Also: `turn`, `history` (input items), `segment_start_turn`, `turn_limit`, `read_limit`, `token_limit`, `segment_reads`, `segment_tokens`, `refused_submissions`, `resumed_at_turns`, `transcript_id` and `plan`.
31|   - `status` is `running | submitted | needs_input`.
32|   - `SessionStore`: `save`, `load`, `append_transcript(transcript_id, record)`, `transcript(transcript_id)`. Implementations: `MemorySessionStore()` (`fleetsre/sre/session.py`) and `SqliteSessionStore(path)` (`fleetsre/adapters/sqlite_state.py`).
33|9. **`investigate(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, max_turns=24, max_read_calls=12, max_tokens=400_000)`.**
34|   - With no saved session it starts one. With a saved `running` session it continues it with the budgets passed. With a saved `submitted` or `needs_input` session it raises `ValueError`.
35|   - `resume(incident, tools, gateway, store, *, message, extra_turns=8, extra_reads=4)` raises `ValueError` unless the saved session is `needs_input`.
36|   - Both return `InvestigationResult(diagnosis, status, reason, transcript_id, turns, read_calls, tokens, refusals)`. `status` is `submitted`, with `reason` the submitted action type (`propose` or `none`), or `needs_input` with a reason from pin 15. For `escalated`, `diagnosis` is set.
37|10. **`ModelGateway(config, transport, *, sleep=time.sleep)`.**
38|    - `ModelGateway.respond(role, input_items, tools)` returns `ModelResponse(output, usage)`; `tools` may be `None`.
39|    - `Transport.create(request: dict) -> dict` raises `TransportError(status)`.
40|    - `ScriptedTransport(responses)` records `.requests`; an item `{"_error": <status>}` raises `TransportError`.
41|    - `GatewayConfig.prices`: per model, USD per 1M tokens (`input`, `cached_input`, `output`).
42|    - `OpenAITransport(*, api_key, base_url)` calls the OpenAI SDK's `responses.create` with SDK `max_retries=0` and `timeout=120`. A timeout surfaces as `TransportError(504)`. The key is passed explicitly from `MODEL_API_KEY`.
43|    - The live role comes from `FLEETSRE_INVESTIGATE_MODEL` (default `muse-spark-1.3`), effort `medium`, prices from `FLEETSRE_PRICES_JSON`.
44|11. **Gate signatures.** `check_hypotheses(items)`; `check_evidence(args, session, log_query, incident, registry)`; `check_diagnosis(d, session, incident, contract, log_query, registry)`.
45|
46|## Loop
47|
48|12. **Input.** `[developer message: prompts/investigate.md verbatim, user message: render_incident] + history`.
49|    - Request flags: `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`, `reasoning={"effort": role effort}`, `tools=specs()`, `model` = role model.
50|    - Output items are replayed as returned (`exclude_none`).
51|13. **Tool outputs.** Every `function_call` gets a `function_call_output` whose `output` is the string `json.dumps({"callId", "result"})`. Only the first call in a response runs. The others get the error `not run: only the first tool call in a response runs`, and don't count as calls or toward stuck. A reply with no tool call gets the user message `Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool.` and counts as a turn.
52|14. **Last turn.** When `turn == turn_limit`, the user message `This is your last turn. Call submit_diagnosis now with what you have.` is appended before the request, after any plain-text message.
53|15. **Budgets are per segment.** The first investigation is segment 1, and each resume starts a new one.
54|    - Turns: `max_turns`, then `extra_turns`.
55|    - Reads: `max_read_calls`, then `extra_reads`. Only accepted calls to the eight read tools count. A read over the cap is refused (`reads.cap`) and still counts as a turn.
56|    - Tokens: `max_tokens`, counted from the segment start as usage input + output. The check runs after each turn; an accepted submission on that turn wins.
57|    - Three refused submissions in a segment end with `needs_input`/`refused`.
58|    - After a turn, the order is: accepted submission, then the refusal cap, then the token budget.
59|    - The refused-submission count and the stuck counts reset at each resume.
60|    - `needs_input` reasons: `escalated`, `refused`, `budget`, `token_budget`, `stuck`, `model_unavailable`.
61|16. **Stuck.** A read tool called with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time within a segment ends with `needs_input`/`stuck`, before the call runs. Only executed calls count (verdict `accepted` or `wouldRefuse`). Working tools never trip it: repeating one changes session state, and three identical refused submissions reach the refusal cap instead.
62|17. **Backoff.** 429 and 5xx retry with delays of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 s (no jitter), up to `max_retries`, then `needs_input`/`model_unavailable`. Any other `TransportError` → `model_unavailable` at once. Other exceptions propagate.
63|18. **Transcript.** One record per turn, saved with the session after every turn. Each record holds the output items, the tool, args, verdict (`accepted | refused | wouldRefuse | no_tool_call | stuck`), problems, the output, usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cached_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`) and `cost_usd`.
64|
65|## Tools
66|
67|19. **`query_logs(deployment, window, filter, rationale)`.**
68|    - `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}`, relative to `clock.now()`.
69|    - `filter` is `{component?, event?, minSeverity?, runId?}`, `additionalProperties: false`. A `component` that is not a component ID of the deployment's contract is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
70|    - Returns `{"entries", "total", "truncated"}`: newest first by timestamp, at most 50. Each entry is compact: `insertId`, `timestamp`, `severity`, `labels`, `jsonPayload`, `container`.
71|    - Querying a sibling deployment marks it queried.
72|20. **`get_resource(name)`** is GET only. `name` must match an `environments`, `integrationInstances`, `connectorInstances` or `jobInstances` pattern under the fixed prefix (mocks §4.1). Anything else, including `:` custom methods and `/logs/` paths, is refused (`tool.name`) with no HTTP call. Mock errors pass through as an accepted `{"error": <Google error body>}`.
73|21. **Log and test tools.** `list_connector_logs(name)` and `list_job_logs(name)` take full resource names and return one page of 50, newest first: `{"logs", "truncated"}`. `test_integration_instance(name)` takes integration instance names only and returns the `executeTest` body.
74|22. **`compare_siblings(service, component, window)`**, where `window` is `{"lastMinutes": 1..360}` as in pin 19. For each deployment of the service it returns: runs, runs at or above WARNING, ERROR runs, the last heartbeat's timestamp and insertId, alerts ingested, and the insertId of the worst recent entry. It marks every sibling queried. An unknown component is refused (`tool.name`), listing the valid IDs.
75|23. **`tripwire_history(deployment)`** reads the `StateStore`. **`get_contract(service)`** returns the contract JSON with every tripwire `description` removed, plus a scorecard summary only (`passed`, `expected_hit_rate`, `false_positives`, `scenarios: <count>`), with no scenario IDs.
76|24. **Specs.** `submit_diagnosis` carries the full §6.5 schema with its `required` lists (diagnosis, action, `expectedVerification`, `openQuestions` items) and `condition` enum `["recovers_within"]`. `record_evidence`'s `source` is `{insertId}` or `{callId, field, value}`. Every schema has `additionalProperties: false` and a required `rationale` (`maxLength` 200). `update_plan(plan, rationale)` records the plan and has no gate.
77|
78|## Gates
79|
80|25. **Problem strings** take the form `<rule>: <text>`. Rules:
81|    - Order and hypotheses: `order`, `hypotheses.count`, `hypotheses.alternative`, `hypotheses.id`.
82|    - Evidence: `evidence.insert_id`, `evidence.deployment`, `evidence.future`, `evidence.call_id`, `evidence.field`, `evidence.value`, `evidence.hypothesis`, `evidence.limit`.
83|    - Diagnosis:
84|      - `diagnosis.schema`, with the JSON path of the problem (`diagnosis.schema: action: 'type' is a required property`). Argument-validation errors inside `diagnosis` use this rule, not `args.schema`.
85|      - `diagnosis.evidence`
86|      - `diagnosis.coverage`
87|      - `diagnosis.category` (includes `unknown` without `escalate`)
88|      - `diagnosis.action` (method outside the allowlist; empty `escalationSummary`)
89|      - `diagnosis.update_mask` (mask outside the method's fields, or patch keys outside the mask)
90|      - `diagnosis.resource`
91|      - `diagnosis.incident` (`incidentId` or `deployment`)
92|      - `diagnosis.component`, listing the contract's component IDs
93|      - `diagnosis.hypothesis`
94|      - `diagnosis.verification` (missing, or a tripwire not of this deployment)
95|      - `diagnosis.none_after_resume`
96|    - Other: `reads.cap`, `tool.unknown`, `tool.name`, `tool.error`, `args.schema` (with the JSON path).
97|26. **`set_hypotheses`.** Items are `{id, statement, wouldConfirm, alternative}`, all four required. IDs match `^H[1-9][0-9]*$` and are unique. 2–4 items, at least one alternative. Replacing the set keeps evidence whose hypothesis ID remains.
98|27. **`record_evidence`.**
99|    - **Log source:** the insertId exists, its timestamp is ≤ now, and it routes (via `Registry.route`) to the incident's deployment or to a sibling queried in this session (via `query_logs` on it, or `compare_siblings`). There is no other fallback.
100|    - **Tool source:** `callId` is an accepted read-tool call of this session. `field` is a dotted path into the result, where numeric segments index lists and a leading `result.` is stripped. `value` must match by JSON equality, with no coercion.
101|    - At most 3 items per hypothesis. IDs are `E<n>`, and `recordedAtTurn` is the session turn.
102|28. **`submit_diagnosis`** checks, in addition to spec §6.5:
103|    - The schema first. A schema problem always refuses, gates on or off. With gates on and no hypotheses yet, the order problem is reported first.
104|    - `incidentId` and `deployment` equal the incident's.
105|    - `component` is a component ID of the deployment's contract.
106|    - `hypothesis` is a current hypothesis.
107|    - For `propose`: a `connectorInstances.*` method needs the deployment's connector instance name, and a `jobInstances.*` method its job instance name, by exact match. The integration instance is never a valid resource. The patch keys are within `updateMask`.
108|    - `expectedVerification` is required for `propose` and `none`, and optional for `escalate`.
109|    - For `none`: an item counts as recorded after the last resume iff `recordedAtTurn > max(resumed_at_turns)`. With no resume, every item counts.
110|    - Repeated submissions to the ToolSet are allowed; the loop ends at the first accepted one.
111|29. **Category rules** (the spec §6.5 table, tightened):
112|    - `connector_stalled` / `job_stalled`: the cited log evidence includes, by insertId, the deployment's latest heartbeat at or before `trip_event.at`. The heartbeat is the event of the cadence tripwire on the contract's `connectorInstance` (`jobInstance`) component, whatever the incident's component, so a canary incident can be diagnosed `connector_stalled`.
113|    - `credential_failure`: an entry from the deployment's connector at or above WARNING, plus a `test_integration_instance` call on the deployment's own integration instance with `successful: false`.
114|    - `schema_drift`: an entry that routes to the incident's deployment and for which `evaluator.tripwires.schema_violation` returns a reason. `schema_violation` applies the tripwire's `event`/`where` filters itself; `${param}` is resolved.
115|    - `job_hollow_success`: a `job.run.completed` of the deployment with `status: SUCCESS` and `indicatorsSynced: 0`.
116|    - `job_failing`: a `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` with `status: ERROR`, of the deployment.
117|30. **`verification=False`.** The order, hypotheses, evidence and diagnosis rules 2–5 record `wouldRefuse`, with their problems, instead of refusing. Schema problems (`args.schema`, `diagnosis.schema`) still refuse. Budgets, the read cap and stuck still apply.
118|31. **The right component** for evaluation is the tripped tripwire's component.
119|
120|## Recording and evaluation
121|
122|32. **`make record FAULT=<F>`** runs one live investigation on the scripted fixture's world and writes `fixtures/recorded/<F>.json`, containing `{fault, seed, t0, faults, incident, responses, transcript, diagnosis}`. 96|    from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
97|    from fleetsre.evaluator.engine import Evaluator
98|    from fleetsre.mock.world import World
99|    from fleetsre.ports import MemorySink
